description: Single source of truth for the kit's prerequisites (tools, MCP servers, session skills). Read by scripts/preflight.sh (phase 0); cited by README.md and skills/migrate-legacy/SKILL.md. `level` is the migration-pipeline gate: required = phase-0 hard fail, recommended = documented degradation. `requiredBy` lists the skills that hard-require the entry at their own preconditions step; `token` is the string CI expects in each of those skills' compatibility frontmatter (tests/skills/check-frontmatter.py). `requiresSdk` (optional, on an `mcps` entry) is the minimum .NET SDK MAJOR that server's own launcher needs, which may be higher than the pipeline's floor: below it the server cannot start, so scripts/preflight.sh names the floor instead of reporting the setup fine. An entry without the field is unaffected — absent is not "floor 0". `launcher` (optional, on an `mcps` entry) is the executable that starts that server, spelled as .mcp.json invokes it and always a bare command name rather than a path: its absence from PATH proves the shipped launcher cannot have started the server, so preflight probes it with `command -v` and reports the miss — `requiresSdk` is then the remedy that explains what to install about it. An entry without the field gets no probe and behaves exactly as before. Both fields are read by preflight only — hooks/roseline-gate.sh reaches the same conclusion for itself with a hardcoded `command -v dnx`, since a PreToolUse hook cannot afford to parse this file on every C# Read; tests/roseline/test.sh pins that hardcoded name to the `launcher` declared here, so the necessary duplication cannot drift. `tracker` (optional, on a `tools`/`mcps` entry) names the tracker this entry is specific to (e.g. `github`) — scripts/preflight.sh resolves the profile's own Tracker line once and skips an entry whose `tracker` names a different one, so a GitLab or Azure DevOps consumer is never told a GitHub-only CLI is missing. An entry without the field is checked exactly as before, on every tracker. `for` (optional, on a `tools` entry) names the ONE caller that asks for it (e.g. `run-all-tests`) — scripts/preflight.sh skips an entry carrying `for` unless invoked with a matching `--for <name>`, so a fixture-only prerequisite like the .NET 6 runtime never reaches a consumer's phase 0. An entry without the field is checked on every call, exactly as before. Add or remove a prerequisite HERE, never in a hard-coded list. Values must not contain tab characters (tab is the internal field separator).

tools.name: dotnet SDK >= 8
tools.hint: install an LTS .NET SDK — the migration pipeline needs it; the lifecycle skills do not

tools.name: python3
tools.hint: required by the kit's scripts (inventory, dashboard)

tools.name: PyYAML
tools.hint: required by tests/skills/check-frontmatter.py and scripts/ci-wiring-check.py to parse skill frontmatter and workflow YAML, and by skills/setup-repo/scripts/parse-manifest.py to read a repo-setup manifest — CI installs it in a step instead of declaring it, so its absence used to read as dozens of failing tests rather than one missing prerequisite

tools.name: jq >= 1.6
tools.hint: required by hooks/roseline-gate.sh, hooks/git-write-gate.sh, hooks/routing-context.sh and hooks/autodev-stop-gate.sh — without it all four exit silently: C# Reads stop being routed to roseline, destructive or unguarded git writes stop being routed to the guarded-*.sh scripts, the kit's skill-routing table stops reaching sessions outside this repo, and the auto-dev Stop gate can never see a fleet's undrained work. The floor is >= 1.6: skills/implement-issue/scripts/tick-plan.sh's round-trip check uses --rawfile, which older jq lacks

tools.name: glab CLI (authenticated)
tools.hint: GitLab publishing (create-issue's tracker backend, scripts/tracker/gitlab.sh) — only checked on a GitLab profile, never on a GitHub one

tools.name: node / npx
tools.hint: Tailwind CSS (rewritten UIs), and the archify renderer the migration phases draw the architecture with (node bin/archify.mjs) — this entry is load-bearing twice over, so its absence costs both the rewritten UI's styling and the architecture diagram, which falls back to a mermaid fence

tools.name: Chrome headless
tools.test: command -v google-chrome || command -v chromium || test -x '/Applications/Google Chrome.app/Contents/MacOS/Google Chrome'

tools.name: .NET 6 runtime
tools.hint: the frozen samples/LegacyShop fixture targets net6.0 and dotnet test launches it on that runtime — an SDK >= 8 builds it but cannot run it (framework_version=6.0.0 … app-launch-failed). Install the .NET 6 runtime, or run scripts/run-all-tests.sh --quick to skip that one gate; CI's setup-dotnet installs 6.0.x

mcps.name: RoselineMCP connected
mcps.hint: shipped by the tagout-migrate plugin via its .mcp.json (the tagout lifecycle plugin launches no server) and launched with dnx, which needs the .NET 10 SDK even though the pipeline itself accepts >= 8; usage is enforced by hooks/roseline-gate.sh, disable with ROSELINE_GATE=off (mandatory for all C# analysis)

mcps.name: AdrMcp connected
mcps.hint: shipped by the tagout-migrate plugin via its .mcp.json (the tagout lifecycle plugin launches no server) and launched with dnx (.NET 10 SDK); optional — create-issue, implement-issue and merge-pr fall back to reading docs/adr/*.md frontmatter and say so

mcps.name: context7 MCP connected
mcps.hint: recommended: up-to-date docs for the target frameworks

sessionSkills.name: archify
sessionSkills.when: before drawing a legacy app's architecture — phase 1, the executive audit, the report; degrades to the mermaid fence the phase already writes
